newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Megawati supporters stage protest in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Megawati supporters stage protest in Jakarta.

text.p: Several hundred supporters of Megawati Sukarnoputri staged a low-key demonstration in Jakarta on Thursday in protest against the man who ousted her as leader of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
About 300 demonstrators handed a petition to a parliamentary official and then drove in a motorcade along the city's main thoroughfare to national police headquarters.
Security was light, with only about 20 uniformed policemen in the foyer of parliament's office building.
A squad of about 50 riot police were on guard at police headquarters, a complex of three-storey, cream-coloured buildings about four km (2.5 miles) from the legislature.

The number of demonstrators was far below the 2,000 to 3,000 leaders had predicted for the protest, the first organised opposition political demonstration in Jakarta since July 27 riots rocked the city.
Political observers had said the turnout could give some idea of opposition power in the run-up to general elections at the end of next May.

Police directed traffic and escorted about 40 carloads of demonstrators to the police complex, where staff Lieutenant-Colonel I Made Dharma received a petition from Roy Janis, chairman of Megawati's PDI faction in Jakarta.
The demonstrators, many in red and black PDI colours, shouted and waved from their cars, but they got little response from people on the streets.

The demonstration was called to demand authorities investigate the activities of deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi, who replaced Megawati as PDI leader at a government-backed rebel congress in June.
President Suharto has given Surjadi his seal of approval, and only members of his faction have been approved to run for the PDI in the elections.

The demonstrators had wanted to hand their petition to parliament's speaker Wahono, but he and other senior officials refused to see them. The petition was finally given to the head of parliament's public relations section.
Organisers said they planned to drive on to Surjadi's home from police headquarters.
Political analysts have said the government wanted Megawati out of the PDI because of her potential vote drawing power which might hit the ruling Golkar party in the May polls.

The July riots, in which at least five people died and dozens of buildings burned or damaged, were sparked by an attack by Surjadi backers on the PDI headquarters occupied by loyalists of Megawati, daughter of Indondesia's founding president Sukarno.
Police charged 124 Megawati supporters with disobeying orders and refusing to disperse, but made no move against Surjadi's backers in the attack on the PDI building.
Last month, 115 of those arrested were released after serving four months in jail. Nine others were acquitted.
A number of those sentenced were among the demonstrators on Thursday, and several had to be restrained by colleagues when they started shouting at senior police officers.
The official National Commission on Human Rights in a report on the July 27 events criticised the government for not treating both sides equally.

In the Thursday petition, the protesters said the government should take appropriate action equally against both PDI groups. It called for the temporary suspension of Surjadi's position in parliament and demanded that Megawati supporters be allowed to contest the elections.
